reason: Six requirements implemented across four new modules with 55 tests in the EP-008 suites and 433 passing workspace-wide. The most significant finding is a gate weakness rather than a feature: the pack validator checked only `verdict == PASS` on anti-gaming reviews, so five of this session's own reviews satisfied the gate while missing 19 of the 20 fields the shipped schema requires. The check now enforces the schema, proven load-bearing by a 7-case negative proof, and the five reviews plus EP-001's six-line stub were rewritten to comply.
real_vulnerabilities_found: The generated-pack validator trusted a single string field on anti-gaming reviews. Five reviews (EP-003 through EP-007) passed the gate with 19 of 20 required evidence fields absent, and EP-001's review was a six-line note. This is precisely the 'evidence sticker' failure DONE_LAW.md warns about, and the gate could not detect it.
EP-000 and EP-002 have no anti-gaming review at all. They are reported as warnings rather than silently accepted, and are NOT claimed as verified by this node.
known_limitations: The crash bundle assembles and renders in memory. Wiring it to a real panic hook, to disk, and to the upload path is desktop-shell work that remains outstanding; no end-to-end capture-from-a-real-panic claim is made.

The repair broker models the workflow and its gates as a state machine. It does not create a real git worktree or invoke a real coding agent; the GitHub integration does not exist and no PR has been opened.

EP-000 and EP-002 remain without anti-gaming reviews. They were closed by a prior session and this node does not attest to their evidence quality. EP-002's recorded unit-tests exit code is 1 with no corresponding log, which is a pre-existing anomaly this node surfaces but does not resolve.
REQ-039 (SLOs) and REQ-041 (SBOM and license gate) remain PENDING and are not claimed here.
Structured events and health states are implemented and tested; the health UI that would display them is part of the desktop shell work.
